design_intent.original_text: Make it a 3x3x3 cube with no gravity: players still alternate placing X and O in any empty cell; any straight line of three cells through the cube (rows, columns, pillars and every diagonal, 49 lines in total) wins; a full cube with no line is a draw.
preserve: Players alternate placing X and O.
A player may place a mark only in an empty cell.
changes: Allow placement in any empty cell without gravity.
A straight line of three cells through the cube wins, including rows, columns, pillars, and every diagonal; there are 49 winning lines in total.
A full cube with no winning line is a draw.

lift_plan.source_xy_policy: Keep the existing bounded x and y axes at extent 3, their coordinates, initial empty cells, X-first turn order, and empty-cell placement rule. Do not add gravity.
lift_plan.neighborhood: For winning lines, use all straight three-cell directions through the cube: three axis directions, six face-diagonal directions, and four body-diagonal directions. These define 49 distinct winning lines: 27 axis lines, 18 face diagonals, and 4 body diagonals. Placement itself has no neighborhood restriction.
lift_plan.movement: On a turn, the current player places their mark at any empty (x,y,z) cell. Reject an occupied cell or a placement after the game ends without changing state. Players continue alternating unless the placement ends the game. Restart resets all 27 cells and the turn to X; quit remains a host command.
lift_plan.outcomes: After each legal placement, a player wins if their marks fill any of the 49 straight three-cell lines. Check the win before the draw. If all 27 cells are occupied with no winning line, the result is a draw.
lift_plan.presentation: Show the board as the engine-owned continuous cube volume, with X and O in their cells and the existing turn, win, or draw status. Do not split the cube into panels.
lift_plan.input: Clicking a cell supplies its full (x,y,z) coordinate. The engine's existing '[' and ']' keys and on-screen buttons select depth for picking inner cells. Keep restart and quit bindings.
z_equals_one_tests: With z at extent 1, the same x and y placements, turns, and occupied-cell rejections must behave as in the Source.
With z at extent 1, only the Source's eight rows, columns, and diagonals can win; a full board without a line is a draw.

z_gt_one_tests.name: same x and y on different layers are distinct cells

source_game_spec.summary: Two players alternate placing X and O on a 3×3 grid; three in a row wins, and a full board without a win is a draw.

initial_setup.description: Every cell is empty; X moves first, with no winner or draw.

actions.legal_when: There is no winner or draw, x and y are each within 0 through 2, and board[y][x] is empty.
actions.effect: Set board[y][x] to the current player's value. Check for a win, then a draw; only if neither occurs, switch the current player from 1 to 2 or from 2 to 1. An illegal placement returns false without changing state.

actions.legal_when: An R keydown is received; the source imposes no game-state restriction.
actions.effect: Reset the board, current player, winner, and draw state to their initial values.

actions.legal_when: Escape is pressed or a window-close event is received.
actions.effect: Stop the application loop; no game outcome is assigned.

outcomes.condition: After a placement, any row, column, or either diagonal has all three cells equal to the current player's value.
After a placement, no winning line exists and every board cell is nonzero.

controls.control: Left-button down; convert pointer position to a cell using the board's left and top offsets and cell size.

presentation.description: A Pygame window displays a status line showing the turn, winner, or draw; instructions; and a 3×3 board of rounded cells with blue X marks and orange O marks. The display loop is capped at 60 frames per second.
